units: SI: metres, seconds, kilograms, newtons, pascals unless a key says otherwise
frame: the model's: +Z towards the muzzle, +Y up, +X to the shooter's left; origin on the bore axis at the receiver front face
time_zero: the sear releasing the hammer (the trigger break); ignition follows after lock_time

barrel_length.source: maker's specification for the 20 in model (notes/REFERENCES.md)

test_barrel_length.source: published shotshell velocities are taken to be 30 in test-barrel figures (industry practice; the load pages do not say)

shell_mass.source: one loaded 2 3/4 in shell: payload + wad + charge + about 9 g of hull and head

payload_start.source: distance from the breech face to the base of the wad before firing

chamber_len_equiv.source: gas volume behind the wad at shot start, as a length of bore

gamma.source: ratio of specific heats of propellant gas, a usual textbook value

p_peak.source: peak pressure of the fitting curve, 9,000 psi (the tracks scale it up by about 14 % so the 20 in barrel delivers the published speed): below the 11,500 psi maximum average pressure of the industry standard for 12 gauge 2 3/4 in (figure recalled from ANSI/SAAMI Z299.2, not re-read)

p_start.source: pressure at which the payload starts to move

gas_velocity_factor.source: SAAMI "Gun Recoil Formulae" (2018): propellant gas leaves at 1.5 x muzzle velocity for shotguns of average barrel length

lock_time.source: sear release to ignition; the manual gives no figure

stroke.source: the forend's rear is 100.4 mm from the receiver face in the profile photo; 97.5 mm used so the bolt stays inside the receiver (model/build.py)

lost_motion.source: slide travel that unlocks the bolt before the bolt moves

hull_fired_len.source: a 2 3/4 in shell is 2 3/4 in long after firing (the nominal length)

shell_loaded_len.source: typical loaded length of a 2 3/4 in shell

tube_capacity.source: maker's specification: 9 rounds in all with 2 3/4 in shells, one of them chambered; manual p8: one fewer with 3 in shells

stroke_time_back.source: game tuning: a brisk rearward stroke

stroke_time_forward.source: game tuning: a brisk forward stroke

stroke_exponent.source: slide position = stroke x (t / T)^1.6: the hand accelerates into the stop

source.payload: published: Federal Power-Shok F127 00, nine lead .33 in pellets at 11.35 g/cc = 31.5 g
source.charge: guess: a typical charge for this class of load; makers do not publish it

source.payload: published: Federal Power-Shok F127 RS, 438 gr

manual.safety: p5: the button on the top rear of the receiver; rearward is ON (SAFE), forward is OFF (FIRE). p20: with the safety ON the hammer does not fall when the trigger is pulled
manual.action_lock: p6: the action lock lever, left side behind the trigger guard, lets the action be opened without pulling the trigger. p9: it must be depressed to eject an unfired shell
manual.loading: p8: open the action and put the first shell through the ejection port (into the chamber or onto the elevator), then close it. p9: load the magazine with the action closed, pushing each shell in until its rim snaps past the cartridge stop
manual.cycling: p9: pulling the forearm completely rearward ejects the case through the ejection port. p10: pulling it completely rearward releases the next shell onto the elevator; pushing it fully forward chambers the shell
manual.unloading: p10: with the action closed, depressing the cartridge stop through the loading port releases shells from the magazine one at a time
manual.function_test: p20: safety ON, pull: no fire. Release, safety OFF: no fire. Pull: the hammer falls. Open the action, safety ON
manual.takedown: pp. 10 to 14: magazine cap and barrel; trigger housing pin and housing; cartridge interrupter and stop; bolt slide; bolt; elevator; forearm and action slide

mass.note: part masses are mesh volume x material density (model/inventory.json), scaled so the total is the published 7.25 lb; each part is a box of its bounding size at its bounding-box centre

events.name: unlock
events.what: the bolt lock is down: the bolt starts to move

events.name: hammer_cocked
events.what: the bolt slide has pushed the hammer back onto the sear

events.name: extracted
events.what: the fired hull's mouth is out of the chamber (hull length of bolt travel)

events.name: eject
events.what: the hull meets the ejector and leaves through the port (manual p9)

events.name: shell_released
events.what: the cartridge stop lets the next shell onto the elevator (manual p10: "completely rearward")

events.name: rear_stop
events.what: the slide stops at the rear

events.name: lift_start
events.what: the elevator starts to rise as the slide starts forward

events.name: lift_done
events.what: the shell is in line with the chamber

events.name: feed
events.what: the bolt face meets the shell head and pushes it forward

events.name: chambered
events.what: the shell is home and the bolt stops

events.name: locked
events.what: the bolt lock is up, the slide is forward, the action lock engages (manual p10: "fully forward")

profile.formula: back: s = S (t / Tb)^e. forward: s = S (1 - ((t - Tb - Td) / Tf)^e)

kinematics.note: the same numbers as the model's pump clips (model/build.py)

hull.source: guess throughout (game tuning): the hull leaves sideways at about 1.2 x the slide speed, a little up and back, tumbling; restitution and friction by surface

free_recoil.formula: SAAMI: gun mass x speed = ejecta mass x muzzle velocity + charge mass x 1.5 x muzzle velocity; gun unloaded, 7.25 lb

barrel_20in_estimate.note: what this pressure curve gives in 20 in when fitted to the published speed in 30 in. A model estimate that depends on the guessed curve; not used for the tracks

free_recoil.formula: SAAMI: gun mass x speed = ejecta mass x muzzle velocity + charge mass x 1.5 x muzzle velocity; gun unloaded, 7.25 lb

barrel_20in_estimate.note: what this pressure curve gives in 20 in when fitted to the published speed in 30 in. A model estimate that depends on the guessed curve; not used for the tracks

buck00_muzzle_velocity.note: a calibration: the pressure curve is scaled to deliver the published speed

buck00_impulse.note: the force on the gun integrates to the SAAMI recoil momentum

buck00_peak_pressure.note: below the 11,500 psi industry maximum average pressure (recalled figure)

buck00_shoulder_gun_speed.note: a held gun peaks a little under the free recoil speed

buck00_hip_gun_speed.note: a held gun peaks a little under the free recoil speed

slug_muzzle_velocity.note: a calibration: the pressure curve is scaled to deliver the published speed

slug_impulse.note: the force on the gun integrates to the SAAMI recoil momentum

slug_peak_pressure.note: below the 11,500 psi industry maximum average pressure (recalled figure)

slug_shoulder_gun_speed.note: a held gun peaks a little under the free recoil speed

slug_hip_gun_speed.note: a held gun peaks a little under the free recoil speed

stroke_clears_hull.note: the bolt travels further than a fired 3 in hull is long, as it must to eject one (manual p8: 3 in shells are allowed)

tube_holds_published_capacity.note: modelled tube length (cartridge stop to the inside of the cap) less a guessed 45 mm for follower and compressed spring, over a 59 mm shell. An independent check of the photo ruler
